question: On the desolate, rust-colored plains of Kepler-186f, a collective of extraterrestrial artisans, comprising both Zorgon master-builders and Flarb apprentices, are commissioned to construct a complex, modular cosmic harmonizer. A highly skilled Zorgon can independently fabricate one module in precisely 12 hours, while a less seasoned Flarb requires 18 hours to produce an identical module.  If an assembly team is composed of 5 Zorgon master-builders and 9 Flarb apprentices, and their current directive is to assemble 10 modules of this intricate cosmic harmonizer, calculate the total time, in hours, it will take for the entire team, working concurrently and maintaining their individual production rates, to fulfill this cosmic construction endeavor.
title: Cosmic Harmonizer Module Assembly Time for Zorgons and Flarbs
solution:
Work rate of a Zorgon master-builder = 1 module / 12 hours
Work rate of a Flarb apprentice = 1 module / 18 hours
Number of Zorgon master-builders = 5
Number of Flarb apprentices = 9
Combined work rate of 5 Zorgons = 5 * (1/12) = 5/12 modules per hour
Combined work rate of 9 Flarbs = 9 * (1/18) = 1/2 modules per hour
Total combined work rate of the team = (5/12) + (1/2) = (5/12) + (6/12) = 11/12 modules per hour
Number of modules to assemble = 10
Time taken to assemble 10 modules = Total modules / Combined work rate = 10 / (11/12) = 10 * (12/11) = 120/11 hours
Time taken = ~~120 / 11 = 10.9090...~~ hours
Rounded to 2 decimal places, Time taken = 10.91 hours
